* * *
 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed claim application U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
(SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 On 18.10.2024 the petitioner was driving the Canter bearing No.KA-01-AJ-0941 which was loaded with Plywood towards Tumkuru on the extreme left side on Bengaluru - Tumkuru NH-48 Road, while so proceeding at about 10.00 p.m, reached near Veerus Residency Hotel, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru, the said canter's front right tyre punctured, due to which the petitioner lost control and said vehicle went on road divider and stopped, hence the petitioner got down and was standing behind of the said canter, giving directions to other coming vehicle to pass, at that time, suddenly the driver of Lorry bearing No. TN-40-W-9034 came from Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and behind left portion of the said canter, consequent to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Abhay Vasishtha hospital,
Madanayakanahalli, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 18.10.2024 to 28.10.2024 and has undergone surgery and discharged with an advise for follow-up treatment, not to involve in any strenuous activities and for complete bedrest and as per the advice of the doctors the (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 petitioner is still continuing follow-up treatment and so far he has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 37 years and was earning his livelihood as Driver in his own canter vehicle and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
On account of A/K amputation right knee, the petitioner is completely bedridden and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending lorry by its driver and in this regard the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of the said lorry.

Hence,
the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with cost and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, was placed exparte.

On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and Chandan Kumar Ray Alias Chandan Kumar vs Baranitharan S on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23904975/
2 has filed objections.
(SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 04.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending lorry, age, income, occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint and the alleged accident caused due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and the contributory negligence is more on the part of the petitioner and there is no fault, rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the lorry.

The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties and this respondent denies existence of policy to the offending car which is pending confirmation from the concerned branch of this respondent and the liability if any is subject to terms, conditions and limitations of the policy and the owner of the Lorry bearing No.TN-40-W-9034 has not immediately reported the occurrence of the accident to this respondent and has not submitted the claim forms and other documents and he has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and the driver of the said lorry was driving the vehicle without possessing a valid (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 and effective driving licence, FC and Permit and hence there is violation of policy conditions, Rules and Regulations of M.V. Act.

The compensation claimed is highly excessive and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against the respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 18.10.2024 at about 10.00 p.m, on Bengaluru-Tumakuru NH-48 Road, near Veerus Residency Hotel, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-40-W-9034 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether respondent No.2 proves that driver of lorry has not having valid license?
03. Whether respondent No.2 proves that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner vehicle?

04. Whether respondent No.2 proves that petitioner Canter No.KA-01-AJ-0941 owner and insurance company are necessary parties?
(SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 05.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
Chandan

06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 submits no evidence.
Hence, the respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard arguments.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1
In affirmative  Issue No.2 In the Negative  Issue No.3 In the Negative  Issue No.4 In the Negative  Issue No.5 In partly affirmative  Issue No.6

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel

,
but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Nelamangala Traffic Police against driver of the Lorry.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the lorry the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.3 is Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident on NH-48 Express Road, near Makali, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident and damages caused to its front and rear side.

Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate shows petitioner sustained right leg crush injury type III compound fracture right leg with ripped muscles with cut lacerated wound anterior middle 1/3rd upto ankle exposed muscles vessel, contamination and above knee amputation done and said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P.6 is the Charge sheet filed against driver/respondent No.1 of the offending lorry for rash and negligent driving for (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 the offences punishable U/Sec 281, 125(b) of BNS.
Ex.P.7 is Aadhaar card of petitioner.
Ex.P.8 is Disability ID card of petitioner.

Ex.P.9 is Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner sustained right leg crush injury, type III compound fracture right leg with ripped muscles contamination from M/3rd thigh with contamination with CLW extended from anterior aspect M/3rd thigh upto ankle exposed muscles, bones with contamination and edge necroses with fat necrosis of A/K amputation right knee and Ex.P.12 is Artificial limb quotation.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Lorry the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.2 has not lead Chandan Kumar Ray Alias Chandan Kumar vs Baranitharan S on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23904975/
4 evidence.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issues No.2 to 4:-

In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
12.

The respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that the accident occurred due to the (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 negligence of the petitioner vehicle and driver of the lorry was not having valid licence and petitioner has not made owner and insurer of his canter vehicle as necessary parties.

On perusal of Charge sheet it is found that the canter vehicle tyre was punctured and was stopped for repair and driver was giving signal to other vehicles to pass sideby on the road,
at that time the driver of lorry came from behind and dashed to the petitioner's canter, which shows rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the lorry and further in Charge sheet has not quoted any sections regarding non-possessing of driving licence by the driver of the offending lorry.

When the accident was occurred by the driver of offending lorry, the question of impleading owner and Insurance Company of the petitioner's canter as parties does not arise and in this regard the respondent No.2 has not examined any of the witnesses to prove its contention.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.2 is acceptable.
Accordingly, Issues No.2 to 4 are answered in the negative.

13. Issue No.5:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of (SCCH-3)
11 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 37 years and was earning his livelihood as Driver in his own canter vehicle and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m and and has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,.
On account of A/K amputation right knee, he is completely bedridden and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature.

14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate,
school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.7 Aadhaar card.
Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the same can be relied upon,
According to which, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1987.
The alleged accident occurred on 18.10.2024.
Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 age of petitioner is 37 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 37 years as on the date of accident.

15. As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and as per Ex.P.9 Discharge summary the petitioner was admitted as inpatient at Abhay Vasishtha hospital for 10 days.

But in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to show that he has sustained any physical or functional disability which is come in the way of his day to day life.
As per Ex.P.10 the petitioner has incurred Medical expenses of Rs.2,67,273/-.

Absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner Chandan Kumar Ray Alias Chandan Kumar vs Baranitharan S on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23904975/
5 sustained any physical or functional disability and no evidence on record to show his age, avocation and income.

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained loss of future income and loss of income during laid up period and also there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner requires further treatment.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,70,000/-.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,70,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
17. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

On service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but it has not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.5 partly in affirmative.
18. Issue No.6:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

(SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7971/2024 The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,70,000/- (Rupees Three lakhs and seventy thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
